title: Rabbi Natan Daroma
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin, chapter 6, end of halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.6.4.5) relates that Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yonatan went up to Chamat Gader and decided to wait for the elders of the South. Rabbi Natan Daroma came; they asked him and he permitted it. Resh Lakish heard and responded, etc. Hyman calls this a scribal error: the reading should follow the account in [Babylonian Eruvin 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.65b.15-18) about Resh Lakish and Rabbi Chanina’s students, who asked Rabbi Afes. As Hyman explained in his entry, although Rabbi Afes headed the academy in Tzippori after Rabbi’s death, under Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi’s patriarchate, his permanent home was in the South. Hyman finds no Rabbi Natan Daroma elsewhere.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Jerusalem Talmud prints Peres in parentheses and Natan in brackets before Daroma. Its translator reports that two responsa quote the name as Afes.

The linked Bavli separately names Rabbi Afes as the sage consulted after the rental. Hyman argues that Afes should replace Natan in the Jerusalem Talmud passage and that Afes’s permanent home was in the South.
